tasks.short: Forecast workforce needs and employment costs under agreed business scenarios.

steps.what: Agree business demand, planning assumptions, and staffing constraints.
Export current positions, vacancies, employee costs, and planned departures.
Reconcile workforce totals and map positions to departments and cost centres.
Calculate staffing and cost scenarios using demand, attrition, and recruitment assumptions.
Challenge scenarios with department managers and resolve staffing trade-offs.
Approve the workforce forecast for inclusion in the financial plan.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {HCM}, {ATS}, and {PAYROLL} feed a reconciliation job on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, joined to cost centres from the {ERP}. A deterministic scenario generator feeds the {BI} and creates a forecast pack in the {DOCS}; managers challenge assumptions and the finance director approves adoption.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workforce and cost data use different identifiers and dates. Rebuilding reconciliations and scenario workbooks makes changes slow.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, scheduled jobs, and parameterised calculations support this already. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building mappings and scenario generators.
tasks.still_hard: Business demand, attrition, and productivity remain uncertain. A mathematically consistent forecast can still use poor assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Managers judge operational constraints and negotiate trade-offs between cost, capacity, and service.

ambition.what: Monthly comparison of recruitment versus internal redeployment for capacity gaps.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding workbooks and more time testing staffing choices with department managers. They gain faster scenario access; headcount approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess internal redeployment before requesting new positions.
reach.learn: Learn position planning, skills constraints, and consultation requirements.

reach.task: Estimate whether training can close a forecast capability gap.
reach.learn: Learn training lead times, completion capacity, and realistic time to proficiency.

evidence.claim: Structured workforce data supports deterministic reconciliation and parameterised staffing scenarios.
The digest supports deterministic dashboards and calculations for HR planning, with managerial judgement retained.

assumptions: This is aggregate workforce planning, without individual employee ranking or automated employment decisions.
Configured exports are available; custom connectors would increase integration effort.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges estimate working-day effort for one entity; national consultation calendars may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Which workforce forecasts the reward team owns rather than finance or wider HR.
Whether position, employee, vacancy, and cost centre identifiers reconcile.
Which export permissions, planning tools, and consultation arrangements exist.
Who can approve forecast adoption and subsequent headcount changes.
research_questions: Which forecasting assumptions produce useful improvements over the previous planning baseline?
What aggregation and retention rules satisfy GDPR and applicable national rules?
Would any proposed individual-level extension change the EU AI Act classification?
new_work: Resolve unmatched positions and cost centres.
Maintain scenario parameters and cost assumptions.
Back-test forecasts against actual staffing and costs.
Review access permissions and changes to source schemas.

tasks.short: Maintain personnel records and produce consistent workforce statistics.

steps.what: Record approved hires, transfers, departures, and other employee changes.
Extract employee movements, absence totals, and appraisal completion records.
Reconcile identifiers, effective dates, duplicates, and missing fields.
Investigate discrepancies and correct source records using approved evidence.
Calculate headcount, movement, absence, and appraisal completion statistics.
Check unusual totals and approve the report for its intended audience.

tasks.design: Configure approved employee changes in the {HCM}, then feed the {HCM} and {TALENT} into a validated personnel dataset on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic metrics populate the {BI}; configured access controls and disclosure rules restrict audiences, while the {WORKFLOW} routes source corrections and report approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent definitions, effective dates, and permissions force manual reconciliation. Existing reporting features may also be poorly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Established reporting, validation, and workflow features cover most of this task. AI-assisted coding makes small reconciliation jobs cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Historical corrections and conflicting source records need evidence. Small groups can reveal sensitive information even in aggregate reports.
tasks.human_edge: People resolve ambiguous records and judge whether a report is fair, meaningful, and appropriate for its audience.

ambition.what: A privacy-filtered workforce movement briefing for department managers.

tasks.altitude: Routine exports and calculations leave the week. The manager spends more time resolving meaningful discrepancies and explaining workforce changes; access and employment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve employee record discrepancies at their source.
reach.learn: Learn effective dating, evidence requirements, and correction audit trails.

reach.task: Reconcile employee movements with payroll population changes.
reach.learn: Learn payroll cut-offs, retroactive changes, and population reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Configured record workflows, validation rules, and scheduled reporting can handle structured personnel administration.
GDPR requirements apply to personnel reporting; absence detail may require special-category safeguards.

assumptions: Employee changes have already received their required employment approvals before automated recording.
Absence reporting uses totals and excludes medical narratives.
Reporting covers appraisal completion, without automated performance scoring.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges estimate working-day effort; national employee consultation may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Which record maintenance is performed by the reward team or shared HR services.
Whether approved employee changes can flow directly into the HCM.
Which metric definitions, historical corrections, and audience permissions are agreed.
Which national consultation requirements and employee representation arrangements apply.
research_questions: Which disclosure controls preserve useful reporting while reducing re-identification risk?
What source reconciliation checks detect material errors before report release?
Does the proposed reporting scope remain outside high-risk employment AI uses under the EU AI Act?
new_work: Investigate validation exceptions and disputed corrections.
Maintain metric definitions and effective-date rules.
Review access, retention, and small-group disclosure controls.

tasks.short: Investigate personnel problems and recommend evidence-based changes to policies and practices.

steps.what: Define the personnel problem, affected groups, and questions requiring investigation.
Assemble relevant workforce, pay, and policy information for the agreed scope.
Compare trends and groups, checking denominators, uncertainty, and plausible confounders.
Test explanations with managers and employee representatives where appropriate.
Draft improvement options with evidence, costs, uncertainties, and proposed evaluation measures.

loop.input: Approved aggregate findings, reviewed discussion notes, policy excerpts, and an option template.
loop.output: A cited options draft separating observations, hypotheses, costs, and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Validate figures against supplied tables and references against source IDs; the manager reviews reasoning.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unsupported claims remain flagged and incomplete sections return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but synthesising varied explanations and policy text requires bounded language drafting.

steps.what: Select recommendations for further consultation or a defined policy pilot.

tasks.design: A deterministic pipeline joins approved personnel data and payroll totals on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with repeatable comparisons in the {BI}. A bounded drafting loop assembles cited options in the {DOCS}; people test explanations and approve recommendations before consultation or pilot implementation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fragmented data and repeated analysis consume time. Statistical associations also need organisational context that report templates cannot supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable statistical code can generate consistent comparisons. Bounded drafting can turn reviewed evidence and policy extracts into a traceable first draft.
tasks.still_hard: Observational data rarely establishes causes. Small samples, missing context, and competing interests can make recommendations uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: The manager distinguishes plausible explanations from convenient stories and builds support for a proportionate response.

ambition.what: Evaluation of a targeted retention-policy pilot against an agreed comparison group.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time investigating causes and designing evaluations. They can propose smaller, testable interventions sooner; policy and employment approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess consultation and collective-agreement implications of a proposed policy change.
reach.learn: Learn representative engagement, national rules, and collective-agreement interpretation.

reach.task: Assess whether a proposed reward policy creates unequal effects.
reach.learn: Learn defensible group comparisons, confounding, and equality impact assessment.

evidence.claim: Deterministic statistics can support personnel analysis, but causal interpretation and policy selection require human judgement.
A documented job-evaluation pilot reported above 70% agreement with experts on 50 job descriptions; this does not validate causal personnel analysis.
A documented workplace study reported 2.8% time savings from chatbots, cautioning against assuming large realised savings.

assumptions: The tool analyses aggregate patterns and does not rank employees or decide employment outcomes.
The model receives minimised aggregate evidence and reviewed notes, excluding raw medical or grievance narratives.
Recommendation approval does not replace any consultation or approval required before a policy takes effect.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover working-day effort for an initial analytical scope; consultation may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Which personnel problems the reward team is expected to investigate.
Whether reliable historical data and suitable comparison groups exist.
Which analytical skills and policy evaluation practices are already available.
Which employee representatives, data permissions, and policy approval routes apply.
research_questions: Which proposed analyses can support causal claims, and which support only descriptive findings?
Does the intended analytical use fall within EU AI Act employment provisions?
What GDPR safeguards and national consultation steps apply to the selected policy pilot?
new_work: Review drafted claims, citations, and uncertainty statements.
Maintain metric definitions and analysis code.
Investigate apparent disparities and conflicting explanations.
Monitor pilot outcomes and unintended effects.
Reassess privacy and legal scope when new data or uses are added.

tasks.short: Select and contract suppliers for employee services.

steps.what: Agree employee service needs, service standards, budget, and selection criteria.
Prepare the supplier request using service requirements and standard terms.
Approve recipients and send the supplier request.
Read supplier proposals and capture prices, exclusions, service levels, and contract departures.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and a fixed schema for rates, units, exclusions, service levels, and departures.
loop.output: Structured offer fields with source passages and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Validate schema, currency, units, and source references; a person verifies material commercial fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per proposal; unreadable or ambiguous fields go to procurement.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents vary in wording and layout; fixed parsers cannot reliably interpret exclusions and departures.

steps.what: Calculate comparable service costs and score offers against agreed criteria.
Negotiate service quality, pricing, implementation, and employee protections with shortlisted suppliers.
Review contractual, privacy, liability, and service-continuity terms.
Approve the supplier commitment and sign the service contract.
Register the contract, service owner, renewal dates, and purchasing references.

tasks.design: Configure request templates and approvals in the {PROCUREMENT}; a bounded extraction loop converts proposals from the {DOCS} into cited offer fields, followed by deterministic cost comparisons. People negotiate and review the contract, the authorised signatory commits through the {ESIGN}, and configured flows populate the {CLM} and renewal schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier proposals use inconsistent formats, while terms and approvals sit across documents and mailboxes. Employee service quality also depends on context that price tables miss.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing purchasing and contract workflows handle templates, approvals, and renewal dates. Bounded extraction can reduce document reading without delegating negotiation or commitment.
tasks.still_hard: Service reliability, accessibility, liability, and employee trust need judgement. Bespoke contract terms and provider data access remain expensive to resolve.
tasks.human_edge: The manager represents employee needs, tests supplier credibility, and negotiates workable commitments.

ambition.what: An accessible transport service option for employees working late shifts.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time preparing comparisons and chasing contract records, leaving more time for service design and supplier discussions. Negotiation and signature authority remain within existing delegated limits.

reach.task: Plan employee communication and enrolment for a new service.
reach.learn: Learn eligibility rules, accessible communication, and service onboarding.

reach.task: Assess consultation needs when an employee service changes.
reach.learn: Learn collective commitments, national consultation rules, and representative engagement.

evidence.claim: Templates, approval workflows, deterministic offer comparisons, and renewal records can automate contracting administration.

A documented supplier-negotiation case reported agreements with 68% of approached suppliers and 3% average savings; it concerns different purchases and does not establish suitability for employee services.

assumptions: The manager negotiates within delegated limits; binding commitments require the authorised signatory.
Configured purchasing, contract, and signature workflows are available.
The comparison uses reviewed offer fields and agreed criteria; it does not automatically award contracts.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges estimate working-day effort for one service category; employee consultation may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Which employee services and supplier categories the reward team owns.
Which purchasing thresholds, signature limits, and legal review requirements apply.
Whether providers receive employee personal data and under which contractual arrangements.
Which service changes require consultation under national rules or collective agreements.
Whether existing systems support the required approval and contract registration flows.
research_questions: Which proposal fields can be extracted reliably across representative supplier documents?
Which employee service criteria predict service quality beyond price?
What GDPR roles, transfer safeguards, and national consultation requirements apply to the selected service?
new_work: Verify extracted prices, exclusions, and service commitments.
Maintain request templates, comparison formulas, and approval thresholds.
Handle missing offers, non-standard terms, and integration failures.
Review supplier performance and renewal alerts.
Maintain service eligibility and privacy requirements as services change.

role.altitude: The role shifts from assembling records and packs towards testing reward and workforce choices, investigating unequal outcomes, and shaping employee services. Employment, policy, budget, and contract decisions retain their existing human approval routes.
reach: Partner with human resources managers on workforce redeployment options.
Partner with training and development managers on capability gaps.
Partner with labor relations specialists on consultation and collective commitments.
Partner with equal opportunity representatives on policy impact assessment.
skills_to_grow: Workforce scenario modelling and forecast evaluation.
Statistical reasoning, causal inference, and uncertainty communication.
Personnel data definitions, effective dating, and privacy-aware reporting.
Review of model drafts and source-linked extractions.
Employee consultation, service design, and supplier negotiation.
role.ambitious_version: Run a recurring workforce and reward review that compares staffing options, tests targeted policy pilots, and evaluates employee service access using trusted aggregate evidence.
